<description>
`mining_prioritisetransaction.py` checks that `prioritisetransaction` alone makes `getblocktemplate` return a new block, by comparing the whole template before and after moving mocktime 10 seconds forward. But `curtime` comes from the clock, so the two templates always differ, even if the template wasn't rebuilt.

This PR checks that the deprioritised transaction drops out of the template instead.
If you remove the counter bump in `CTxMemPool::PrioritiseTransaction` (the fix this check was added for in #10196), the test from master still passes but this one fails.
</description>

[2026-11-20] c:7030937588 comment by Pranav-error:
I verified that the check on master is effectively vacuous. Removing the `prioritisetransaction` call still makes the test pass (exit 0), while the PR correctly fails with an AssertionError. A mutation removing `++nTransactionsUpdated` is also caught by the PR but passes on master.

The issue is that `curtime` gets refreshed even when the cached block template is reused, so the existing check never actually verifies the intended update. The PR also relies on the +10s mocktime bump, without which its test fails.

These results confirm that the PR makes the test meaningfully validate the transaction prioritisation behavior.
</new_statements>
